thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: multiple alerts firing for inference-queue-latency across us-west/region-1. PD INC assigned (INC-1861). Root metric looks like a bursty upstream retry loop. Posting here to coordinate mitigation and handoff.

Marta: seeing a very short-lived spike, ~3 mins, lots of 503->retry chatter from the batcher. No large customer error rate increases in the customer-errors dashboard (only retries).

Jon: confirmed — traffic backpressure from a model rollout caused queue depth to jump. A lot of noise from per-host alert rules. Can we group by model_id+region and lower noise?

Simon: we should avoid paging on each host. Proposed immediate live mitigation: 1) create composite alert that aggregates across model_id+region; 2) temporary 10m suppression window for host-level alerts during bursts; 3) downgrade severity for retry-only blips. Thoughts?

Marta: agree. For immediate action I can patch the alert rule to change "for" to 2m -> 5m and add a grouping key. Doing a quick patch now.

Ops Bot: Deploy bot: created temporary alert override (id=ovr-792). Patch applied to rule "inference-queue-latency-host" -> group_by: [model_id, region] and for: 300s.

Jon: nice. Also adding a dedupe key in PD to avoid one page per host. PD manual suggested config: group_on: "fingerprint:{{model_id}}:{{region}}". I'll open a PD change now.

Liz QA: quick note on customer impact — we saw 0.8% increased retries for api-prod-prod from 13:02-13:06, no user-facing errors. Logging indicates backoffs recovered after 4 mins. Recording for post-incident notes.

Marta: adding an on-call runbook step to route noise like this to a "non-paging" channel if it matches these conditions (delta <1% users failed, only retry metric bumped). Draft snippet: 

```
# Alert funnel rule (temporary)
if metric == inference-queue-latency and group_by in [model_id, region] and customer_error_rate < 1% and spike_duration < 10m:
    severity = elevated-batch
    route = #alerts-non-paging
    pd_grouping = fingerprint:{{model_id}}:{{region}}
```

Simon: suggest also adding a short-term router rule to fallback to a cheaper model variant during the spike to buy time. Not for immediate paging mitigation but for next steps.

Jon: created PD rule change request: https://pagerduty/changes/CHG-9323 — sets dedupe to fingerprint-based grouping and adds 5m cooldown. Also added rate-limit on notifications (max 1/min per fingerprint).

Marta: FYI I'm going to create a small dashboard widget (alert funnel) to track "alerts prevented by grouping" and a quick chart of retries vs customer errors. That will help us decide whether permanent rule changes are needed.

Ops Bot: Dashboard patch deployed: dashboard id dash-453, widget added: "inference alert funnel".

Jon: For the post-incident work items — I'm capturing these: 
- Create a long-lived composite alert grouped by model_id+region (priority: medium)
- Add PD dedupe fingerprint for model_id+region and 5m cooldown (priority: high)
- Add a suppression window for host-level pages during known rollout windows (policy)
- Add alert-funnel dashboard panel + SLA impact time series (owner: Marta)
- Runbook update: criteria for non-paging routing and examples (owner: Simon)

Marta: assigning follow-ups in our tracker now. I'll also add a short retro note to the incident ticket summarizing that customer impact was minimal and mitigation prevented noisy paging.

Simon: handing off overnight watch to Jon. If anything spikes again, use the PD change request to temporarily silence and escalate if customer error rate > 1%.

Jon: taking handoff. I'll be on-call for the window 20:00-08:00 PST. Ping me in #eng-oncall with @Jon if you need me. :thumbsup:

Incident Bot: Note: will auto-close PD silence (ovr-792) at +10m unless extended.

Liz QA: adding a quick smoke checklist to verify no regression after rollouts (send sample requests, check latency, check customer-errors).

Marta: thanks all — follow-up ticket: INF-Noise-1861 created and linked to the PD incident. We'll use that to track permanent tuning and add the grouping to our alert templates.

Jon: +1. If we see this pattern repeatedly during rollouts, next week we should consider smarter rollout throttles to avoid queue backpressure.

Simon: closing thread for live mitigation; reopening after the retro if needed. :white_check_mark:
